crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Invoice Capture and Coding
children.blurb: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices from paper, PDF, email and electronic formats, the extraction of header and line item data, and the assignment of general ledger accounts, cost centres, tax codes and project or department dimensions.

children.name: Customer Credit Risk
children.blurb: Customer credit risk in payables and receivables covers the likelihood that a customer will fail to pay an invoice on time or in full.

children.name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
children.blurb: Programmable settlement and escrow covers systems that hold funds or payment instructions and release them automatically when predefined conditions are met.

children.name: Collections and Payment Plans
children.blurb: Collections and payment plans in the AI Accountant covers the systems that manage overdue invoices, schedule customer payments, and decide when to escalate or offer revised terms.

children.name: Working Capital Timing
children.blurb: Working capital timing covers the deliberate scheduling of cash inflows from receivables and outflows to payables to shorten the cash conversion cycle.

sections.body: This field covers the money a business owes and is owed. AI is now doing real work in invoice handling: reading PDFs and emails, extracting supplier names, amounts, dates, line items, and matching them to purchase orders. In receivables, machine learning models score customers for late payment risk using payment history, public filings, and industry data. Settlement systems use rules and small language models to reconcile bank statements and flag mismatches. Collections teams use AI to draft reminder emails and suggest payment plans based on a customer's past behavior. Working capital tools forecast daily cash positions from open invoices and expected payment dates.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Invoice capture is largely solved for clean, digital invoices in common formats, but handwritten, scanned, or multi-language invoices still need human review. Credit risk models are useful for ranking customers, but they cannot predict sudden insolvency or fraud, and they inherit bias from historical data. Programmable settlement works well for simple, rule-based escrow releases, but complex contractual conditions still require manual approval. Collections automation can send polite reminders and track promises to pay, but it cannot replace negotiation with a distressed customer. Working capital timing forecasts are reliable over short horizons, less so beyond a few weeks, because they depend on customer behavior that no model fully knows.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how raw supplier documents become accounting entries should start with Invoice Capture and Coding, which covers extraction, validation, and general ledger mapping. Customer Credit Risk explains the models and data sources used to decide how much credit to extend and when to tighten terms. Programmable Settlement and Escrow shows where money movement can be automated through smart contracts or bank APIs, and where it cannot. Collections and Payment Plans covers the outreach, dunning, and installment logic that sits after an invoice is overdue. Working Capital Timing ties the others together by showing how payables and receivables affect daily cash, and what levers change the timing of inflows and outflows. Together these pages move from recognizing a bill to getting paid, with risk and cash as the connecting threads.
